D: The Pevensies return to Narnia, centuries later, to help Prince Caspian against his tyrant uncle.
P: Serve the snacks when the Pevensies find the apple trees at the ruins of Cair Paravel.
S: Red and green apple slices with warm honey peanut butter
Red and green apples sliced and fanned on a board around a dip of peanut butter loosened with honey, dusted with cinnamon.
Self-raising bread with rubbed in butter, scored and baked
Damper of self-raising flour, butter and milk baked at 200C for 30 minutes, torn and served with butter.
Reepicheep, the bravest mouse in Narnia

Little scones packed with vintage cheddar and chives, baked tall and golden with a cheesy crust, split and spread with cold butter. Rub 60g cold butter into 350g self-raising flour with a pinch of salt and half a teaspoon mustard powder. Stir in 120g grated vintage cheddar and a handful of chopped chives, then 250ml milk to make a soft dough. Pat out 3cm thick and cut 12 small rounds. Brush with milk, top with 30g more cheese and bake at 220C for 12 to 14 minutes until risen and golden. Serve warm with butter.
M: Lamb shoulder simmered with pearl barley, carrots, leeks and rosemary
Lamb shoulder, barley, carrots and leeks simmered 2 hours in stock with rosemary, with crusty bread.

Pork loin rubbed with fennel seed and garlic, roasted at 200C for an hour with apples and potatoes, sliced with pan juices. Score the skin of a 1.5kg boneless pork loin and pat dry. Crush 2 tsp fennel seeds with 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp salt and pepper and rub into the meat, then rub the skin with oil and salt. Roast at 220C for 25 minutes, then 180C for 40 minutes. Add 800g potatoes in chunks for the last 60 minutes and 4 halved apples for the last 30. Rest 10 minutes, slice and spoon over the pan juices.
W: Cinnamon green apples under an oat crumble
Apples cooked with butter and cinnamon under an oat crumble, baked at 180C for 35 minutes, with custard.
K: Milk whisked with dark chocolate, malt powder and brown sugar

Dark chocolate melted into hot milk with malted milk powder, whisked frothy and topped with whipped cream and a sprinkle of malt. Heat 1L full cream milk until steaming. Whisk in 120g chopped dark chocolate, 4 tbsp malted milk powder and 1 tbsp brown sugar until smooth and frothy. Pour into 4 mugs, top each with a spoon of whipped cream and a pinch more malted milk powder.

dishes.make_ahead: Slice the apples within the hour so they do not brown; the peanut butter and honey can be mixed up to 2 days ahead and warmed to serve

steps.text: Slice the apples and fan them on a board.
Warm the peanut butter with honey until loose.
Spoon into a bowl in the middle and dust the apples with cinnamon.
Heat the oven to 200C. Rub the butter for the dough into the flour and salt.
Mix in the milk with a knife until it just comes together.
Shape into a round and score the top.
Bake.
Tear warm and serve with butter.
Slice the carrots and leeks.
Brown the lamb in oil.
Add the barley, vegetables, rosemary and water and simmer until the lamb is tender.
Serve in deep bowls with crusty bread.
Slice the carrots and leeks and halve the mushrooms.
Brown the mushrooms in the oil.
Add the barley, vegetables, rosemary and stock and simmer until the barley is tender.
Stir in the cannellini beans and warm through.
Serve in deep bowls with crusty bread.

dishes.make_ahead: Cook the apples and rub the topping up to 1 day ahead, stored apart in the fridge; assemble and bake on the night

steps.text: Peel and slice the apples.
Melt the butter for the apples in a pan, add the apples and cinnamon and cook, then spoon into a dish.
Rub the topping butter into the oats, flour and sugar and scatter over.
Bake at 180C.
Warm the custard and serve over the crumble.

s.note: Red and green apple slices with warm honey peanut butter
s.how: Slice 2 red and 2 green apples and fan them on a board. Warm 4 tbsp peanut butter with 2 tbsp honey until loose and spoon into a bowl in the middle. Dust the apples with a little cinnamon. The orchard at the old castle still grows them.

s.note: Self-raising bread with rubbed in butter, scored and baked
s.how: Rub 60g butter into 450g self-raising flour with a pinch of salt. Mix in 300ml milk with a knife until it just comes together. Shape into a round, score and bake at 200C for 30 minutes. Tear warm and serve with plenty of butter.

m.note: Lamb shoulder simmered with pearl barley, carrots, leeks and rosemary
m.how: Brown 1kg diced lamb shoulder, then add 150g pearl barley, 3 sliced carrots, 2 sliced leeks, rosemary and 1.5L water. Simmer for 2 hours until the lamb is tender. Serve in deep bowls with crusty bread for an army hiding underground.

w.note: Cinnamon green apples under an oat crumble
w.how: Peel and slice 5 green apples and cook with 30g butter and cinnamon for 5 minutes. Spoon into a dish. Rub 70g butter into oats, flour and 80g brown sugar and scatter over. Bake at 180C for 35 minutes and serve with warm custard.

d.note: Milk whisked with dark chocolate, malt powder and brown sugar
d.how: Heat 1L full cream milk until steaming. Whisk in 120g chopped dark chocolate, 4 tbsp malted milk powder and 1 tbsp brown sugar until smooth and frothy. Pour into 4 mugs, top each with a spoon of whipped cream and a pinch more malted milk powder.
